title: The System Behind Self-Driving: Waymo’s Dmitri Dolgov

reader_summary.headline: Waymo's Dmitri Dolgov explains how self-driving cars see, learn, and scale safely.
reader_summary.overview: Waymo uses cameras, lasers, and radar to see the world in 360 degrees. The company relies on one large AI model that drives the car, creates training simulations, and judges safety. Success comes from slowly improving the system over twenty years rather than finding a single magical breakthrough.

key_points.text: The car runs its main driving AI locally without needing the cloud for real-time decisions.
key_points.evidence_quote: Nothing's in the cloud? Nothing real time. Nothing real time with the cloud. And there are some things that can happen in the cloud, but they're not required.

key_points.text: A simple system fails on rare dangerous situations, so a simulator and critic are needed for safety.
key_points.evidence_quote: If that's all you do, like, pixels and trajectories out, it becomes very difficult to do all of those three and achieve the high level of safety and performance that we require and it becomes very difficult to kind of do it at scale.

key_points.text: Waymo currently operates about 3,000 cars in 11 US cities, completing half a million rides every week.
key_points.evidence_quote: We have about 3,000 cars on the roads. We're doing about half a million rides per week. That translates to about, you know, over 4 million fully autonomous miles per week.
